COMP-dns.desc: DNS probes: system resolver, --server custom, --doh RFC8484 (hand-rolled wire), literal short-circuit, RCODE surfacing

COMP-tcp.desc: TCP connect probes with classified failure modes (timeout/refused/reset/unreachable) and latency

COMP-tls.desc: TLS handshake with SNI, ALPN, cipher, cert subject/issuer/validity; --insecure mode

COMP-http.desc: HTTPS/HTTP1.1 single request per address over TLS, status/redirect/body-size

COMP-http2.desc: HTTP/2 single request over ALPN h2 connection, protocol identity preserved on failure

COMP-http3.desc: HTTP/3 QUIC probe over UDP path, distinct from TCP path

COMP-probe.desc: Repeated probing with latency stats (min/p50/p90/p95/p99/max/jitter/failure-dist) for tcp/tls/http/http2/http3

COMP-route.desc: Linux UDP/ICMP traceroute, root/CAP_NET_RAW gated, IPv4-only

COMP-diagnose.desc: Deterministic evidence-based diagnostic engine (layer.rs/connectivity.rs/filtering.rs/dns.rs), no network I/O

COMP-model.desc: typed observation model: DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP/latency/probe/diagnosis; serde Serialize

COMP-report.desc: human + --json rendering of all observation types

COMP-lib.desc: public library API: async probe functions with explicit timeouts, bounded concurrency (parallel_map)

DEC-001.rationale: User explicitly prefers 功能性开发为主 (functional-first): ship features + fix bugs + tighten correctness over architecture/docs refactor churn until backlog is drained
DEC-001.alternatives_rejected: architecture polish, extensive doc rewrites, test-only rounds

DEC-002.rationale: Maintain zero-new-dependency pattern: hand-rolled protocol code (DoH wire parser, etc.) reuses in-tree rustls/hyper/hickory/quinn rather than adding deps

DEC-003.rationale: --follow redirects deliberately NOT implemented: a redirect is an observation, the tool does not chase it (README documents this)

DEC-004.rationale: Coverage gate is whole-crate >=80 (currently 93.37%); per-module gaps (http3 ~74%) deferred — diminishing returns, bespoke misbehaving-QUIC fixtures

DEC-005.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): user invoked graph-engineering to start a new milestone. Quality convergence already reached (93.37% cov, all CI gates green); enter FEATURE EVOLUTION mode to deliver user-visible new capabilities.
DEC-005.alternatives_rejected: more quality-convergence rounds on an already-plateaued repo; idle/QUEIESCE

TASK-sni-override.summary: CLI --sni <name> override on tls/http/http2/http3/probe: present a chosen hostname as SNI (+HTTP Host) while probing the resolved target addresses; validates certs for that name even when connecting to an IP literal; library already separates destination from sni

TASK-sni-diagnose.summary: diagnose --sni <name>: run the full probe pipeline presenting a chosen hostname (SNI/Host) instead of the target, so a full diagnosis can be scoped to how a given IP behaves for a given domain

ISS-sni-not-exposed.summary: The CLI exposes no way to override SNI/Host: probing an IP literal (e.g. a CDN edge or --server result) always presents the literal as SNI, and --insecure is required even when the target IP belongs to a known hostname; the library (tls::probe(dest, sni, ...)) already separates destination from sni, so the gap is CLI-only

CHG-sni-override.summary: --sni <name> on tls/http/http2/http3/probe presents the chosen hostname as SNI (+ HTTP Host) while probing the target addresses; human reports now surface the presented name when it differs from the destination literal; 3 fixture-gated integration tests

CHG-sni-diagnose.summary: diagnose --sni <name> presents the chosen hostname as SNI/Host across the full probe pipeline while the target stays the probe set; CLI test pins output surfaces the name and keeps the literal as destination

TASK-path-http.summary:
--path

on http/http2/http3/probe: the probes currently hard-code the request path to /, so path-dependent behaviors (WAF rules, CDN cache keys, per-endpoint certs, health endpoints) cannot be observed; add a path parameter through the library probe fns, model (HttpObservation.path) and report

ISS-path-hardcoded.summary: HTTP/1.1/2/3 probes always request "/", so a user cannot observe how a destination behaves for a specific resource (e.g. /healthz or a path behind a WAF); the method (--method) and hostname (--sni) are controllable but the path is not

TASK-header-http.summary: --header NAME:VALUE (repeatable) on http/http2/http3/probe to send custom request headers (e.g. Authorization, User-Agent, cookie) — currently the probes hard-code user-agent/accept and allow no request customization

CHG-path-http.summary: --path <path> on http/http2/http3 + probe --protocol http*; HttpObservation.path; human report shows non-default path; api-baseline regenerated (probe fns gained a path arg); 2 fixture-gated tests proving wire routing

CHG-header-http.summary: --header NAME:VALUE on http/http2/http3 + probe; headers param through all HTTP probes and repeats; fixture answers 202 on marker header, proving wire delivery on TCP+QUIC; malformed header rejected; api-baseline regenerated

ISS-headers-not-sendable.summary: HTTP probes hard-coded user-agent/accept and allowed no request customization (no Authorization/cookie/etc.), so endpoints requiring a header could not be probed truthfully

TASK-http-headers.summary: Capture and render HTTP response headers in http/http2/http3 observations: currently only status/protocol/location/body-size are recorded, so server-software/CDN/proxy evidence (Server, Via, Alt-Svc, Set-Cookie, cache-control, x-*) is invisible; add a bounded headers list to HttpObservation, render a curated set in report, JSON carries all

ISS-headers-not-observed.summary: The HTTP probes discard the response headers entirely; a user cannot see which server/CDN/proxy answered, how it caches, or what cookies/set-cookie were set — core evidence for network diagnosis (identifying a WAF, a CDN hit, a proxy hop)

CHG-http-headers.summary: HttpObservation.headers captures bounded response headers; JSON carries all, human report shows diagnostic subset; fixture sends server: ip-tools-fixture; tests prove TCP+QUIC capture; api-baseline regenerated (headers field)

TASK-probe-dns.summary: dns --count N: repeat resolution of the target and aggregate per-resolver/per-record-type latency statistics (min/p50/p90/p95/p99/max/mean/jitter) plus success rate and failure distribution, filling the one layer (DNS) without a repeat view; design per DEC-006

ISS-dns-repeat-missing.summary: The probe command aggregates repeated latency/success/failure stats for tcp/tls/http/http2/http3 but not dns — the very first layer the tool measures and often the first to show flakiness or steering. A single dns run shows one-lookup latency; there is no way to see resolver stability over time (p50/p95/jitter of resolution, intermittent SERVFAIL/REFUSED)

DEC-006.rationale: DNS-repeat lands on the dns subcommand (--count N), not probe --protocol dns: ProbeResult.destination is a SocketAddr and the diagnose engine joins repeated probes to addresses by destination, whereas DNS repeat is hostname-centric (per resolver + record type); shoehorning it into the address-sweep probe flow would mislabel rows or silently drop per-resolver detail
DEC-006.alternatives_rejected: probe --protocol dns (address-keyed ProbeResult does not fit hostname resolution); a separate repeat command (more CLI surface for the same capability)

CHG-dns-repeat.summary: dns --count N aggregates per-resolver/per-record-type latency + failure stats via DnsClient::resolve_repeat / dns::aggregate_repeat / DnsRepeatResult; --doh looped; --count 1 default stays single-shot; fake-resolver unit test + 2 CLI tests; api-baseline regenerated

TASK-cert-expiry.summary: tls report surfaces days-until-expiry / expired for the peer certificate (renderer-only, no API churn): the notAfter date is shown but never the actionable remaining-lifetime signal, so a cert expiring in 3 days is invisible without manual date arithmetic

ISS-cert-lifetime-invisible.summary: The TLS report prints the notAfter timestamp but never computes remaining lifetime, so an expiring or expired certificate is not flagged; ops monitoring cert expiry per endpoint requires manual date arithmetic on the raw timestamp

CHG-cert-expiry.summary: tls/http cert row annotates remaining lifetime: (expires in N days) within 30d or (expired); renderer-only via Hinnant day-diff; unit tests for date math + far/near/past

TASK-diagnose-request.summary: diagnose --method/--path/--header: thread the request-control flags the milestone added to http/http2/http3 into diagnose HTTP collection (currently hard-codes GET / with no headers), so the full diagnostic pipeline can be scoped to a specific request (e.g. a /healthz behind a WAF or an authenticated endpoint)

ISS-diagnose-no-request.summary: diagnose gained --sni but its HTTP evidence is always GET / with default headers: a user cannot scope the diagnostic pipeline to a specific method/path/headers, so path- or auth-dependent behavior is invisible to the full diagnosis even though the per-address probes support it

CHG-diagnose-request.summary: diagnose --method/--path/--header thread into collect_http_probes so the HTTP evidence phase is scoped to the request the user cares about (GET / no headers before). 3 flags plumbed through diagnose CLI + mod.rs default wiring; fixture-gated test proving a --header x-fixture-marker reaches the server through the full pipeline (202). 167 tests green, all gates clean. commit afe6b9c

DEC-007.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): DNS-over-TLS (RFC 7858) transport. DoH (RFC 8484) is implemented but the TLS-over-853 DoT transport is missing, so the encrypted-DNS comparison story is incomplete. DoT is a first-class way to query a resolver over an encrypted, tamper-resistant channel and compare its answers against the system/custom/DoH paths side by side (the tool's signature 'compare resolvers to detect steering' capability). Add a repeatable --dot <host[:port]> flag + library dot_query reusing the in-tree rustls stack and the existing DNS wire builder/parser (build_query/parse_dns_response) so no new dependency is added (per DEC-002).
DEC-007.alternatives_rejected: HTTP response-body content capture (sensible next milestone but crosses all three HTTP protocol implementations, larger diff, and body content can be binary/sensitive); batch/multi-host diagnose sweep (new input+aggregation surface, larger scope); DoH-only enhancements (narrower, leaves the TLS transport gap)

ISS-001.summary: DoH (RFC 8484) is implemented, but the DNS-over-TLS transport (RFC 7858, TLS on port 853 with a 2-byte length prefix) is missing: a user cannot query a resolver over a TLS-protected DNS channel and compare it against the system/custom/DoH paths. A resolver or path that is tampered with or blocked at the UDP/plain-TCP level (e.g. an ISP that intercepts port 53) is invisible because there is no encrypted-DNS counterpart to compare other than DoH, and DoT is widely deployed (1.1.1.1:853, 8.8.8.8:853, dns.google).

TASK-001.summary: library dns::dot_query(endpoint, host, record_type, timeout, insecure): open a TCP connection to the resolver, drive a rustls TLS handshake with the endpoint hostname as SNI (port 853 default), send the hand-rolled DNS wire query with the 2-byte length prefix (RFC 7858 framing), read the length-prefixed response, and parse it with the existing parse_dns_response. Model gains ResolverKind::Dot(String). No new dependency (reuses in-tree rustls + existing wire builder/parser).

TASK-002.summary: dns --dot <host[:port]> repeatable flag (like --doh): thread through the dns subcommand single-shot and --count repeat paths, render ResolverKind::Dot rows in render_dns/render_dns_repeat, and document DoT alongside DoH in README. Fixture-gated integration test with an in-process TLS DoT server proving the query reaches it and the A record is parsed.

CHG-001.summary: dns --dot HOST[:PORT] adds DNS-over-TLS (RFC 7858): library dns::dot_query (raw DNS inside TLS on 853, reusing in-tree rustls + existing wire builder/parser, zero new deps), ResolverKind::Dot, CLI --dot threaded through single-shot and --count repeat, report renders DoT rows (human + JSON). parse_dot_endpoint unit test + dot_query doc-test + 2 fixture-gated integration tests (raw query returns canned A/AAAA; --count 3 aggregates 100%). 171 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.32%. commit 26926de

ISS-002.summary: dns --dot added the DNS-over-TLS transport, but diagnose still only folded --doh into its evidence/address pool, so a TLS-protected DNS comparison was unavailable in the full diagnostic pipeline (the diagnosis could not reason over DoT answers or probe DoT-resolved addresses).

TASK-003.summary: diagnose --dot <endpoint> (repeatable, like --doh): fold DNS-over-TLS answers into the full diagnostic pipeline's DNS evidence stack and probed address pool, so resolver-disagreement and steering detection can compare the local/--server path with a TLS-protected channel. Pinned by a fixture-gated test proving diagnose --dot surfaces the DoT-resolved record and renders the diagnosis.

CHG-002.summary: diagnose --dot <endpoint>: folds DoT answers into the diagnostic pipeline's DNS evidence + probed address pool (mirrors --doh). Fixture-gated test proves the DoT-resolved record appears in evidence and the diagnosis renders. 172 tests green, all gates clean. commit b0c5b89

DEC-008.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): HTTP response body content capture. The probes report status, headers and body size but discard the actual response body — yet the body is the decisive evidence for WHY an endpoint behaves as it does (a WAF block page, an auth/JSON error, a rate-limit message, a JS challenge, a captive-portal prompt). Capture a bounded, lossy-UTF8 textual snippet (first 1024 bytes) into HttpObservation and render it in the human report and JSON, completing the HTTP observation. The body is already read for sizing, so this costs no extra I/O and adds zero new dependencies; bounds and explicit truncation keep it safe on hostile/binary bodies.
DEC-008.alternatives_rejected: batch/multi-host diagnose sweep (new input+aggregation surface, larger scope); a --body opt-in CLI flag (extra CLI+API churn when always-bounded capture costs nothing — curl-like tools surface the body); probe --protocol dns (already rejected by DEC-006: dns repeat is hostname-centric)

ISS-003.summary: The HTTP probes (h1/h2/h3) count response body bytes but throw the content away, so a user cannot see WHAT an endpoint actually returned — the body is the decisive evidence for a WAF block page, an auth/JSON error, a rate-limit message, a JS challenge, or a captive-portal prompt, none of which a status code alone reveals.

TASK-004.summary: Capture a bounded lossy-UTF8 textual snippet of the HTTP response body (first 1024 bytes, explicit … truncation) into HttpObservation.body_snippet across http/http2/http3, using the body already read for sizing. Add BODY_SNIPPET_BYTES + a shareable push/serialize helper in http_common.rs. No new CLI flag.

TASK-005.summary: Render HttpObservation.body_snippet in the human report (a body content line) and it already serializes into JSON; update README/CHANGELOG and add tests proving a small body ('ok') is captured and a multi-MiB body is truncated with …, proxied across h1/h2/h3.

CHG-003.summary: HttpObservation.body_snippet captures a bounded (1024-byte, lossy-UTF8, explicit …) textual snippet of the HTTP response body across h1/h2/h3 (reuses the body already read for sizing; zero new deps/flags); human report shows 'body content:' and --json carries it. Report unit test + 2 fixture-gated CLI tests (ok body captured in human+JSON; 2MiB truncated with …). 175 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.47%. commit 5b68c6b

DEC-009.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): HTTP request-body sending. Promote --method/--path/--header already control the request, but there is no way to send a request body, so POST/PUT/API and health endpoints that require a body cannot be probed truthfully. Add --body <TEXT> (repeatable via the shared probe CLI) and a body: Option<&[u8]> parameter through http/http2/http3 probe + repeat library fns and diagnose, sending it on the wire with content-length across all three stacks (h1 hyper Full body; h2 SendStream::send_data; h3 request-stream send_data+finish). No new dependency.
DEC-009.alternatives_rejected: batch/multi-host diagnose (new input+aggregation surface, larger scope); route --json (already implemented); choosing only HTTP/1.1 body support (inconsistent across the three first-class protocols core to the tool); a --body @file reader (can follow later; raw TEXT body is the needed first slice)

ISS-004.summary: The HTTP probes can set method/path/headers but cannot send a request body, so POST/PUT/API and health-check endpoints that require a body (JSON, form data, text) cannot be probed truthfully — the tool can only GET them.

TASK-006.summary: Library: thread body: Option<&[u8]> through http/http2/http3 probe(+/with_roots/+/insecure/impl) and probe::http_repeat/http2_repeat/http3_repeat; send it on the wire with content-length across all three stacks (h1 hyper Full body, h2 SendStream::send_data + trailers, h3 request-stream send_data + finish).

TASK-007.summary: CLI + docs + tests: --body <TEXT> flag on http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose threaded like --method/--path/--header; fixture-gated test proving a POST body reaches the server on each protocol; README/CHANGELOG updates.

CHG-004.summary: --body <TEXT> sends an HTTP request body verbatim on http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose (library body: Option<&[u8]> threaded through probe + *_repeat fns; content-length across h1 Full / h2 SendStream+trailers / h3 stream send_data+finish; diagnose collect_http_probes). Fixture echo.invalid echoes the body; library test proves h1/h2/h3 echo a --body marker, 2 CLI tests (http + diagnose) render it. 178 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.38%. commit 4b2dcd8

DEC-010.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): batch/multi-target diagnosis. diagnose and the probes accept a single target, so an ops/health sweep over many hosts requires a shell loop — one process, one JSON corpus and a single aggregated --strict exit are unavailable. Extend diagnose to accept multiple positional targets, run the full probe+engine pipeline per host sequentially, render each host's evidence+verdicts, emit a JSON array for >1 host (single-host stays the existing object), and aggregate --strict across hosts. No new dependency; single-target output/behavior unchanged.
DEC-010.alternatives_rejected: --interface source-IP binding (real but touches tcp/tls/http/quinn bind paths with higher blast radius); --body @file/stdin (small follow-up to --body, not a milestone); shell-level for-loop batching (no single JSON corpus or aggregated exit)

ISS-005.summary: diagnose and the probe commands accept a single target, so there is no way to run a fleet/health sweep over many hosts in one invocation: an operator must shell-loop, cannot get a single JSON corpus or one aggregated --strict exit status.

TASK-008.summary: Refactor diagnose into a per-target pipeline (probe+engine -> DiagnoseReport) and make the subcommand accept multiple positional targets: run each host sequentially, render every host's DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP/repeat evidence + verdicts, emit a JSON array for >1 host (single-host stays the object), and aggregate --strict across hosts. Unresolvable hosts print their own error and fail the run.

TASK-009.summary: Tests + docs: a CLI test running diagnose on two targets (fixture + a non-resolving host) proving both render and the JSON array / aggregated --strict behave; README/CHANGELOG updates for multi-target diagnose.

CHG-005.summary: diagnose accepts multiple positional targets (fleet/health sweep): each host runs the full probe+engine pipeline sequentially (extracted into diagnose_one); human output renders every host; >1 target emits a JSON array (single stays object); --strict aggregates across hosts; unresolved hosts print their own error and fail the run. No public API change. 2 fixture-gated CLI tests (array + strict). 180 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.39%. commit af58b14

DEC-011.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): multi-target dns (DNS health sweep). diagnose already accepts many targets, but dns — the cheapest layer to sweep — still takes a single hostname, so an operator checking N domains' resolution must shell-loop. Extend dns to accept multiple positional targets, run system/+--server/+--doh/+--dot resolution (single-shot or --count repeat) per host, render every host, emit a per-target JSON array for >1 host (single keeps the flat array), and aggregate --strict across targets. No new dependency; per-target logic factored into dns_compute; single-target behavior/output unchanged.
DEC-011.alternatives_rejected: extending every per-address probe subcommand (tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe) to multiple targets (larger shared run_probe_flow refactor); --interface source-IP binding (touches tcp/tls/quinn bind paths, higher blast radius); --body @file/stdin (small follow-up to --body)

ISS-006.summary: dns accepts a single hostname, so there is no way to run a DNS health sweep over many domains in one invocation: an operator must shell-loop, cannot get a per-target JSON corpus or one aggregated --strict exit for the cheapest layer to check.

TASK-010.summary: Make dns accept multiple positional targets: run system/+--server/+--doh/+--dot resolution (single-shot or --count repeat) per host via a dns_compute helper, render every host, emit a per-target JSON array for >1 host (single keeps the flat array), and aggregate --strict across targets. IP-literal targets keep their no-resolver short-circuit.

TASK-011.summary: Tests + docs: a CLI test resolving two IP-literal targets proving each report renders and --json yields a 2-element per-target array; README/CHANGELOG updates for multi-target dns.

CHG-006.summary: dns accepts multiple positional targets (DNS health sweep): per-host system/+--server/+--doh/+--dot resolution (single-shot or --count repeat) via dns_compute; every host renders; >1 target emits a per-target JSON array (single keeps flat array); --strict aggregates failures across targets; IP literals keep the no-resolver short-circuit. No public API change. 1 fixture-free CLI test (two literals render + 2-element array). 181 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.39%. commit 237cfc1

DEC-012.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): extend multi-target to the per-address probe commands (tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe). diagnose and dns already sweep many targets, but connectivity/latency probes still take a single host, so a fleet connectivity sweep needs a shell loop. Make every probe command accept multiple positional targets and generalize the shared run_probe_flow to loop: resolve+probe each target in turn, label each host block in human output, emit a per-target JSON array for >1 host (single stays flat), and aggregate --strict across targets. No public library API change (cli-private); the probe closure gains a Clone bound so it can be re-invoked per target.
DEC-012.alternatives_rejected: --interface source-IP binding (touches tcp/tls/quinn bind paths, higher blast radius); --body @file/stdin (small DX follow-up to --body, not a milestone); making dns/diagnose multi again (already done in prior milestones)

ISS-007.summary: The per-address probe commands (tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe) accept a single target, so a fleet connectivity/latency sweep over many hosts requires a shell loop — no per-target JSON corpus or one aggregated --strict exit.

TASK-012.summary: Generalize run_probe_flow to accept multiple targets (variadic positional on every probe subcommand via probe_command): resolve+probe each in turn, label each host block in human output, emit a per-target JSON array for >1 host (single keeps flat array), aggregate --strict and unresolved failure across targets. Add a Clone bound on the probe closure so it re-invokes per target.

TASK-013.summary: Tests + docs: a fixture-gated CLI test proving tcp on two loopback targets labels each block and yields a 2-element per-target JSON array; README/CHANGELOG updates for multi-target probe commands.

CHG-007.summary: The per-address probe commands (tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe) accept multiple positional targets: run_probe_flow loops target resolution+probing, labels each host block in human output, emits a per-target JSON array for >1 host (single keeps flat array), aggregates --strict and unresolved-target failure across targets; probe closure gains a Clone bound. No public library API change. 1 fixture-gated CLI test (tcp on two loopbacks labels + 2-element array). 182 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.41%. commit 4927e16

DEC-013.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): --body @file and --body - (stdin). --body shipped accepting a literal string, so large or JSON payloads must be shell-quoted inline. Let --body read from a file (@path) or stdin (-), so payloads can be piped/kept in files. Shared parse_body helper used by http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose; literal behavior unchanged. No new dependency (std fs + io only).
DEC-013.alternatives_rejected: --interface source-IP binding (touches tcp/tls/quinn bind paths, higher blast radius); batch result export CSV/HTML (distinct but larger rendering surface); route multi-target (privileged raw sockets, hard to test deterministically)

ISS-008.summary: --body accepts only a literal string, so a large or JSON request body must be shell-quoted inline — there is no way to read the request body from a file or stdin, which is awkward for multi-line payloads or automated pipelines.

TASK-014.summary: Support --body @<file> and --body - (stdin) via a shared parse_body helper (literal unchanged) in http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose; update --body help text. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test: --body @file and --body - each reach the echo route and are echoed back.

CHG-008.summary: --body @<file> reads the request body from a file and --body - reads it from stdin (literal unchanged) on http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose, via a shared parse_body helper; --body help updated. No public API change, no new dependency. 1 fixture-gated CLI test (@file + stdin each echoed back). 183 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.29%. commit 0e6af0d

DEC-014.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): diagnose --csv. The (now multi-target) diagnose gives rich JSON and human output, but no compact spreadsheet-friendly table; ops want per-host diagnosis rows they can load into a sheet/dashboard. Add --csv emitting header + one row per diagnosis (host,severity,category,confidence,summary), hand-rolled CSV quoting (no new dependency), for single and multi-target sweeps; --strict/unresolved behavior unchanged.
DEC-014.alternatives_rejected: --interface source-IP binding (touches tcp/tls/quinn bind paths, higher blast radius); route multi-target (privileged raw sockets, hard to test deterministically); --header @file/stdin (small DX follow-up, low value)

ISS-009.summary: diagnose (single or multi-target) outputs raw JSON and human text but no compact, spreadsheet-friendly table, so an operator cannot quickly load per-host diagnosis rows (host, severity, category, confidence, summary) into a sheet or dashboard.

TASK-015.summary: Add diagnose --csv: emit a header + one row per diagnosis (host,severity,category,confidence,summary) with hand-rolled CSV quoting, for single and multi-target runs; json/csv/human are mutually exclusive; --strict/unresolved unchanged. Pinned by a fixture-gated CLI test parsing the CSV and checking per-host rows.

CHG-009.summary: diagnose --csv exports each host's verdicts as spreadsheet-friendly rows (host,severity,category,confidence,summary; RFC4180-style quoting), single and multi-target; csv/json/human mutually exclusive; hand-rolled, no new dependency. 1 fixture-gated CLI test. 184 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.31%. commit 2f06ae4

DEC-015.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): --header @file and --header - (stdin). --body already reads from a file/stdin; --header only takes inline NAME:VALUE repeats, so endpoints needing many headers (auth + cookie + custom) must be shell-escaped inline and cannot be reused from a file. Extend the shared parse_custom_headers to expand '@file' (one NAME:VALUE per line) and '-' (stdin line-by-line) in each --header value, applied to http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose. Literal behavior unchanged; no new dependency. Document that '-' consumes all stdin (don't combine with --body -).
DEC-015.alternatives_rejected: --interface/source-IP binding (touches tcp/tls/quinn bind paths + dns sockets, high blast radius, a partial version would be inconsistent); route multi-target (privileged raw sockets, hard to test deterministically); CSV for dns/probe (niche, less actionable than diagnosis CSV)

ISS-010.summary: --header only takes inline NAME:VALUE repeats, so a request needing many headers (auth + cookie + custom) must be shell-escaped inline; there is no way to read headers from a file or stdin for reuse/cleaner automation.

TASK-016.summary: Extend parse_custom_headers to expand '@file' (one NAME:VALUE per line) and '-' (stdin line-by-line) in each --header value, on http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose; literal NAME:VALUE unchanged; clear errors for bad lines/files. Unit tests + a fixture-gated CLI test proving a file's headers reach the server.

CHG-010.summary: --header @<file> reads NAME:VALUE lines from a file and --header - (stdin) reads them from stdin (inline NAME:VALUE unchanged) on http/http2/http3/probe/diagnose; bad file/stdin lines fail clearly. No public API change, no new dependency. 1 fixture-gated CLI test (@file + stdin each deliver the marker header, server answers 202). 185 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.24%. commit 40ee1a6

DEC-016.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): HTTP time-to-first-byte (TTFB). The HTTP probes report total latency (TLS+HTTP) but not the time from sending the request to receiving the response headers — a classic web-performance primitive that separates server response latency from body transfer. Capture ttfb_ms on http/http2/http3 (request-send to headers) into HttpObservation, render it in the human report and carry it in JSON. Zero new deps; the probes already time the overall round-trip.
DEC-016.alternatives_rejected: --interface/source-IP binding (touches tcp/tls/quinn bind + hickory dns, large cross-cutting blast radius, hard to test); route multi-target (privileged raw sockets, not deterministically testable); CSV for dns/probe (format extension, less novel than a new metric)

ISS-011.summary: The HTTP probes report total latency but not time-to-first-byte—the time from sending the request to receiving the response headers—so a slow server response vs slow body transfer cannot be told apart, and a key web-performance primitive is invisible.

TASK-017.summary: Capture ttfb_ms (request-send to response headers) on http/http2/http3 into HttpObservation, render in the human report and carry in JSON; update all HttpObservation test constructors, regenerate api-baseline. Pinned by fixture tests asserting ttfb is present/latent.

CHG-011.summary: HTTP probes (h1/h2/h3) now capture TTFB (HttpObservation.ttfb_ms: request-send to response headers), rendered as 'ttfb:' and carried in JSON, distinct from total latency. 1 fixture test asserts ttfb present and <= latency on all three. Public API note: HttpObservation gained ttfb_ms (api-baseline regenerated). 186 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 93.27%. commit 30f22a1

DEC-017.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): dns --csv. diagnose already has --csv; the multi-target dns sweep (esp --count repeat) gives per-resolver/per-record-type latency stats that ops want in a spreadsheet. Add --csv to dns emitting a uniform row per (host,resolver,record_type): attempts,success_rate,latency_p50/p95/max,failures — single-shot rows are attempts=1, repeat rows use the aggregated stats. Hand-rolled CSV, no new dependency; json/csv/human mutually exclusive.
DEC-017.alternatives_rejected: --interface/source-IP binding (touches tcp/tls/quinn bind + hickory dns, large blast radius, partial version would be inconsistent); route multi-target (privileged raw sockets, not deterministically testable); probe --csv (similar, can be a later follow-up)

ISS-012.summary: dns (including the multi-target --count sweep) emits JSON/human but no spreadsheet-friendly rows; per-resolver/per-record-type latency stats can't be loaded straight into a sheet/dashboard.

TASK-018.summary: Add dns --csv: a uniform row per (host,resolver,record_type) with attempts,success_rate,latency_p50/p95/max,failures (single-shot rows attempts=1; repeat rows use aggregated stats), for single and multi-target; json/csv/human mutually exclusive. Pinned by a CLI test on IP-literal + a repeat case.

CHG-012.summary: dns --csv emits a uniform row per (host,resolver,record_type): attempts,success_rate,latency_p50/p95/max_ms,failures — single-shot rows attempts=1, --count repeat rows use aggregated stats; single and multi-target; csv/json/human mutually exclusive. No public API change, no new dep. 1 CLI test (two literals: header + per-host rows). 187 tests green, all gates clean, coverage 92.72%. commit 52898b2

DEC-018.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): probe --csv. diagnose and dns already have --csv; the multi-target probe --count sweep reports per-address attempts/success_rate/latency percentiles — ideal for a connectivity-health spreadsheet. Add --csv to probe emitting one row per (destination): attempts,success_rate,latency_p50/p95/max_ms,jitter_ms,failures. run_probe_flow gains an optional csv renderer (only probe supplies one, so only probe defines --csv); json/csv/human mutually exclusive. No new dependency.
DEC-018.alternatives_rejected: --interface/source-IP binding (touches tcp/tls/quinn bind + hickory dns, large blast radius, partial version inconsistent); route multi-target (privileged raw sockets, not deterministically testable); tcp/tls/http single-observation CSV (each is one row; less useful than the repeated-probe latency stats)

ISS-013.summary: probe --count reports per-address latency statistics (attempts, success rate, p50/p95/max, jitter, failures) but only as JSON/human text, so a connectivity-health sweep can't be loaded straight into a spreadsheet.

TASK-019.summary: Add probe --csv: one row per (host,destination) with attempts,success_rate,latency_p50/p95/max_ms,jitter_ms,failures for single and multi-target repeated-probe sweeps (--count latency stats); json/csv/human mutually exclusive. run_probe_flow gains an optional csv renderer (only probe supplies one); no new dependency. Pinned by a probe --csv CLI test.

CHG-013.summary: probe --csv emits one row per (host,destination): attempts,success_rate,latency_p50/p95/max_ms,jitter_ms,failures from the --count aggregation, single and multi-target; json/csv/human mutually exclusive (csv wins). No public API change, no new dep. 1 fixture-gated CLI test (header + 3/3 success row). 187 tests green, clippy/fmt/doc clean.

DEC-019.rationale: New milestone (2026-08-22): address-family selection. The per-address probe commands (tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe) resolve each target and probe all of its addresses; a dual-stack host where one family is broken/unroutable forces timeouts and noise, and an operator often needs to test just IPv4 or just IPv6 (is v6 up? probe only v4 of a known-broken-v6 fleet). Add --ipv4/--ipv6 (mutually exclusive) to those commands, filtering resolved destinations by family in run_probe_flow. diagnose deliberately does NOT gain the filter: its address-family asymmetry diagnosis (connectivity.rs family_rules) depends on seeing both families. No public API change; CLI flags only.
DEC-019.alternatives_rejected: extended DNS record types (CNAME/MX/TXT/NS/SOA) — high value but requires redesigning DnsObservation.records from Vec<IpAddr> to a richer DnsRecord model, a public API change rippling through dns.rs/model/report/CSV/diagnostics; park as a separate milestone; --interface/source-IP binding (large blast radius across tcp/tls/quinn bind + hickory); route multi-target (privileged raw sockets)

TASK-020.summary: Add --ipv4/--ipv6 (mutually exclusive) to tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe, filtering resolved destinations by address family in run_probe_flow (default probes all). Pinned by a CLI test: --ipv4 probes an IPv4-literal target and --ipv6 filters it to no addresses. No public API change.

TASK-021.summary: Extend dns beyond A/AAAA to CNAME/MX/TXT/NS/SOA: redesign DnsObservation.records from Vec<IpAddr> to a richer DnsRecord (type + value, MX priority/name) so mail routing (MX), SPF/DKIM (TXT), CNAME/authority (NS/SOA) are inspectable; update report/dns CSV/diagnostics and regenerate api-baseline. Requires public API change; larger, separate milestone.

ISS-014.summary: dns only queries A/AAAA; mail routing (MX), SPF/DKIM (TXT), aliasing (CNAME), and authority (NS/SOA) are not inspectable, so a DNS diagnostics tool cannot answer "where does mail go?" or "does this SPF record exist?".

CHG-014.summary: --ipv4/--ipv6 (mutually exclusive) on tcp/tls/http/http2/http3/probe filter each targets resolved destinations by family in run_probe_flow (default probes all). diagnose deliberately excluded so its family-asymmetry diagnosis sees both families. No public API change. 1 CLI test (ipv4 reaches v4 loopback, ipv6 filters it out, both is a parse error). 189 tests green, clippy/fmt/doc clean.

CHG-015.summary: dns --record-type TYPE queries CNAME/MX/TXT/NS/SOA in addition to A/AAAA (default A+AAAA, --ipv6 stays AAAA shorthand; conflict). DnsObservation.records became a typed Vec<DnsRecord> serializing as plain strings; DnsRecordType gains CNAME/MX/TXT/NS/SOA. hickory lookups decode the new types; DoH/DoT wire parser decodes names/compression-pointers, MX pref+name, TXT strings, SOA fields. diagnostics/report/cli updated; api-baseline regenerated (public API change). Pinned: wire-parser unit tests (CNAME/NS/MX/TXT/SOA), record_from_rdata test, MX/TXT render test, CLI test. 193 tests green, clippy/fmt/doc clean.
